title: A KINGDOM THAT WILL BE EXALTED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Water will flow from their buckets; their seed will have abundant water. Their king will be greater than Agag; their kingdom will be exalted. God brought them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox. They devour hostile nations and break their bones in pieces; with their arrows they pierce them." - Num 24:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's oracle looks ahead to a future for Israel marked by abundance and strength. Their king would be exalted, their kingdom lifted high, all because God had brought them out of Egypt with mighty power. The nation that Balak feared would be established under God's blessing.

We should read these promises rightly. They were spoken to Israel in their particular place in God's redemptive plan, describing the national future God intended for them. They are not a blank cheque of prosperity for believers today. What carries forward is the truth that God is faithful to establish His purposes and exalt His chosen King.

For behind these words lies a hope that reaches beyond any earthly kingdom. The exalted king points ultimately to the greater King who would come from Israel: the Lord Jesus Christ. His kingdom is the one truly lifted high, and it will never end.

This is where our hope rests, not in earthly abundance or national greatness, but in the everlasting kingdom of Christ. He is the King greater than any earthly ruler, exalted to the right hand of God (Phil 2:9-11). Set your hope on His kingdom, which cannot be shaken, rather than on the fleeting powers of this world.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where are you tempted to set your hope on earthly power or abundance?
2. How does the promise of an exalted king point you to Christ?
3. What does it mean to belong to a kingdom that cannot be shaken?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the exalted King whose kingdom will never end. Keep my hope fixed on Your everlasting reign rather than the fleeting powers of this world. Amen.
